# Nonaffine middle translation: coherent source and normal optimization

This is a local theorem for an ACTUAL nonaffine centroid graph, with a freely optimized source and all ambient normals. It is not a global centroid-smoothing theorem. In particular its baseline depth is Gamma_2 of the full mass, above the mixed target Gamma_2/2.

Let

    T=conv{(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)}, |T|=9/2,
    rho>0, c>rho, h=(h1,h2) in R^2.

For real epsilon sufficiently near zero, let C_epsilon be the convex hull of the three fibers

    {-1} x rho T,   {0} x (epsilon h+cT),   {1} x rho T.               (1)

Put

    R=c^2+2rho^2, W=c+2rho, lambda=c/W,
    D=2lambda^2+(1-lambda)^2=2R/W^2.

There is a neighborhood of epsilon=0 on which the true globally deepest point is unique, belongs to the middle fiber, and has the form (0,y(epsilon)), with y smooth. Its raw depth Q(epsilon) satisfies

    y(epsilon)=epsilon lambda h+epsilon^2 y2+O(epsilon^3),
    Q(epsilon)=2R+epsilon^2 q2+O(epsilon^3),                          (2)

where

    q2=D(h1^2+h1*h2+h2^2)/3,
    (y2)_j=[D h_j^2/2-q2]/(2W), j=1,2.                              (3)

All three actual critical continuous normals have zero first variation after this source movement. Their integer tilts are exactly zero in this neighborhood. If h is nonzero, q2>0. Thus any sufficiently small nonzero middle-translation defect strictly raises the true optimized depth at the unchanged total mass (9/2)R. Removing such a defect strictly lowers that optimized normalized depth. This sign is not inferred by freezing the source at its moving own-fiber centroid.

## 1. Actual compatibility, attainment and the baseline menu

The displayed fibers in (1) are exact. Indeed their required midpoint inclusion is

    rho T subset epsilon h+cT,

equivalent by support functions to -epsilon h in (c-rho)T. This holds for all sufficiently small positive and negative epsilon because 0 is interior to T and c-rho>0. The two endpoint bases are exposed; no combination involving the middle can enlarge an endpoint. Every combination giving base zero has its endpoint part in rho T and therefore lies in the displayed middle fiber. The hull is compact, convex and has nonempty ambient interior. Its only integer bases are -1,0,1. Every fiber has positive planar area; translations leave the mixed mass equal to (9/2)R.

At epsilon=0 the exact three-fiber theorem in `candidate f89d52b54ff6950f` gives raw middle-centroid depth 2R. Its complete minimum menu consists of the three canonical directions

    u1=(1,0), u2=(0,1), u0=(-1,-1),                                  (4)

all with integer tilt alpha=0. The canonical endpoint tilt objective has a unique minimizing alpha=0 because its both-proper value is 4rho^2, strictly below the full/empty plateau (9/2)rho^2. The same theorem excludes every other normal, including opposite-canonical and noncanonical mixed-state cuts.

The baseline globally deepest point is unique. At either endpoint the maximum raw depth is 2rho^2<2R, since a finite integer tilt isolates the own ordinary cap. In the middle fiber, for every y!=0, some u_i.y>0. The cap u_i.x>=u_i.y strictly loses middle mass from the canonical cap at zero, while neither endpoint gains mass. Hence its raw mass is less than 2R. This proves strict uniqueness directly.

All through-source minima admit a common compact parameter representation for sources in a bounded neighborhood and all sufficiently small epsilon. Normalize the continuous normal to length one. Once the absolute integer tilt exceeds a common bound, both endpoint traces have their strict full/empty status; replacing that tilt by the bound preserves all three traces. Purely integer caps are dominated by finite nonvertical perturbations: their full middle boundary fiber becomes a proper continuous cap while their strict endpoint statuses stay fixed. Thus the cap mass is minimized on a fixed compact set, including all boundary cases. The mass depends continuously on parameters, source and epsilon; line boundaries have zero area on every positive fiber. Uniform continuity follows on this compact set. These facts give both attainment and uniform convergence of depth functions on the compact, moving middle fibers after translating them back to cT.

The baseline uniqueness consequently localizes every global maximizing source near zero for small epsilon. Otherwise a convergent subsequence of sources outside some neighborhood would have a distinct baseline source of depth at least 2R. The exact endpoint maxima remain 2rho^2 under the translation and are separated from the middle value for small epsilon.

## 2. The full actual cap function near a canonical direction

Around u1, write the normal as (1,theta), allowing theta of both signs near zero, and use one actual integer tilt alpha. At source (0,y), the exact cap volume in its all-one-vertex proper chamber is

    F1(y,epsilon;alpha,theta)
      = sum_(z=-1,0,1)
        [(2-theta)r_z+(1,theta).(c_z-y)+alpha z]^2/[2(1-theta)],      (5)

where r_- =r_+=rho, r_0=c, c_-=c_+=0 and c_0=epsilon h. The formula follows from the two edge intercepts at the common maximizing triangle vertex. Every trace is strictly proper at the baseline and remains so in this open chamber; no clipping formula is omitted locally.

The endpoint contributions in (5) are the squares of the same quantity plus and minus alpha. Therefore the minimizing tilt in this chamber is EXACTLY alpha=0, for every y, epsilon and theta near the baseline. At y=epsilon=alpha=theta=0 the normal-tilt Hessian has entries

    F_(alpha alpha)=2, F_(alpha theta)=0, F_(theta theta)=R>0.         (6)

The ordinary implicit-function theorem supplies a unique smooth critical normal theta1(y,epsilon) near zero. Uniform positive definiteness in a sufficiently small convex parameter chart makes it the unique minimum in that chart. Vertex permutations give the corresponding branches F_i and theta_i for u2 and u0. The permutations are actual linear symmetries of T with absolute determinant one, and they are applied simultaneously to h,y and every continuous fiber coordinate. No integer coordinate is changed.

By the compact parameter representation and the complete isolated baseline minimum menu, all global minimizing caps for a nearby source lie in these three charts. On the compact complement there is a strictly positive baseline gap; uniform continuity preserves a positive gap after small perturbations. Thus, on a neighborhood of (y,epsilon)=(0,0), the TRUE raw depth is exactly

    min{q0(y,epsilon),q1(y,epsilon),q2(y,epsilon)},                    (7)

where q_i is the smooth minimized branch value. There is no normal restriction in (7): the other normals have been excluded by the uniform gap, including pure integer normals and every saturated state. Here q_i denotes a branch function; the scalar q2 in (3) denotes a Taylor coefficient, not the branch with index two.

## 3. A single actual maximizing source and a positive critical circuit

At the baseline, the branch gradients in source coordinates are

    grad_y q_i(0,0)=-2W u_i.                                         (8)

The gradients of q1-q0 and q2-q0 are linearly independent. The implicit-function theorem therefore gives a unique smooth y(epsilon) near zero at which all three branch values agree. Their source gradients remain a spanning positive circuit, since they are continuous perturbations of the three vectors in (8). In particular there is a uniform kappa>0 such that for every unit vector v,

    min_i grad_y q_i(y(epsilon),epsilon).v <=-kappa.

A Taylor estimate with uniformly bounded second derivatives then makes y(epsilon) a strict local maximum of (7): along every nonzero sufficiently small displacement, at least one branch strictly decreases. This is a full directional statement, not only stationarity of an averaged branch.

Depth superlevel sets in the continuous middle plane are convex. Indeed every halfspace containing a convex combination of two points contains at least one of the two points, so depth at the combination is at least their minimum depth. If another point in the middle fiber had depth at least that at y(epsilon), the segment joining them would contradict the just-proved strict local maximum. Hence this is the unique global middle maximum. Together with the separated endpoint values, it is the unique global mixed maximum. It belongs to the original middle fiber by continuity and its baseline interior location.

The branch minimizing caps are precisely the complete critical menu at this source. Their gradients are negative positive section masses times their actual continuous normals, so the positive gradient dependence also gives a positive dependence among those normals. Their integer tilts are zero by (5). These are actual critical caps through one source, not independently chosen formal cap constraints.

## 4. Coherent first and second variations

Write y(epsilon)=epsilon y1+epsilon^2 y2+O(epsilon^3). At the baseline, direct differentiation of (5), followed by the envelope identity at its attained minimum, gives the first-order branch value

    2 u_i.(c h-W y1).

Since all three values agree and sum_i u_i=0, their common first-order coefficient is zero; the spanning property forces

    y1=(c/W)h=lambda h.                                              (9)

Let delta_z be the first-order displacement of fiber center from source. Thus

    delta_-=delta_+=-lambda h, delta_0=(1-lambda)h,
    sum_z r_z delta_z=0,
    sum_z delta_z delta_z^T=D h h^T.                                 (10)

The first-order normal forcing vanishes because of the SAME weighted vector balance. In the u1 chart, differentiation of (5) with respect to theta at theta=alpha=0 gives, for arbitrary small center-to-source displacements d_z,

    F_theta=sum_z r_z[(1,0)+2(0,1)].d_z
              +(1/2)sum_z[(1,0).d_z][((1,0)+2(0,1)).d_z].            (11)

Its first-order term is zero by (10). The same equation after a vertex permutation proves theta_i'(0)=0 for all three branches, since their normal Hessian is R>0. Tilt is already identically zero. Thus optimizing normals makes no second-order correction: their displacement is O(epsilon^2), and the optimized branch agrees with its canonical value up to order two.

At the canonical normal u_i, (5) is simply

    (1/2) sum_z [2r_z+u_i.(c_z-y)]^2.

Using (9)--(10), its order-two coefficient is

    -2W u_i.y2+(D/2)(u_i.h)^2.                                      (12)

All three coefficients equal the common raw-depth coefficient. Summing (12) over i and using sum_i u_i=0 gives

    3 q2=(D/2)[h1^2+h2^2+(h1+h2)^2],

which is (3). The two equations for u1,u2 give the displayed y2 coordinates. The quadratic h1^2+h1*h2+h2^2 is positive for every nonzero h. Smoothness provides the claimed remainders and therefore the strict local sign in (2).

This theorem shows precisely why the ordinary middle centroid is not the right moving source for this variation: its velocity would be h, whereas the true maximizing source velocity is lambda h with 0<lambda<1. It also separates coherent source optimization from frozen-normal computations. No inference of monotonicity for a finite displacement, behavior at midpoint-contact saturation, or elimination of arbitrary nonaffine centroid graphs is made.
